newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures end mostly higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures end mostly higher.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures ended mostly higher, led by a firm technology sector.
March Standard and Poor's 500 futures hit a fresh record at 791.90 after early weakness and Nasdaq 100 futures surged to an all-time high of 935.00.

"I think people really like the situation we're in earnings-wise," one S&P 500 futures trader said. "And the S&P was dominated by Intel and Microsoft, so indeed the tech issues ex-IBM were enough to keep everything going," he said.
In New York Stock Exchange trade, IBM closed down 12 at 157-3/8, dragging the Dow down with it.
Traders tied IBM losses to investor disappointment in the company's fourth-quarter earnings released on Tuesday, but said the overall stock market remained bullish.
Even as Treasury bonds struggled late in the day, S&P 500 futures remained buoyant, traders said.
"We traded off a little bit when bonds put in their low, but then they shut them down and we had a good little bounce," another S&P 500 trader said.
Another trader estimated March S&P 500 futures volume at 85,000 and noted good, solid buyers. He said resistance lurks at 794.15, a trendline on daily bar charts.

A technician noted that March S&Ps recovered from early losses both on Tuesday and Wednesday, each day posting a new record high after the early dip. He said profit-taking and technical setbacks continue to be met with buyers, a good sign for the market.

At settlement, March S&Ps were up 4.65 points to 791.60, KCBT Value Lines were down 0.60 at 707.80, NYSE Composites rose 1.75 to 415.55, Nikkeis were up 500 at 18,145 and Nasdaq 100s were up 13.60 at 933.10.
